bridge_toll_man.text: I remember the ferry from Kyle to Kyleakin. You queued, you waited, and a seagull ate your sandwich. The bridge fixed two of those.
The toll was the worst bit. It cost more than a small car to cross a few hundred yards. A campaign called 'SKAT' got it scrapped in 2004. I joined, for the singing.

storr_guide.text: The Old Man's about 50 metres high, a rock tower with a thin neck and a bad attitude. A path winds up the hillside, and you can see him from the top of the track. In sun, he looks gorgeous. In fog, he looks like a rumour.
The hills here have names in Gaelic: An T-Sràcan, Bodach an Stòrr. 'Bodach' means old man. Whoever named him didn't hang about.

pool_swimmer.text: It's 8 degrees. It's not 'refreshing'. It's a medical event with a nice view.
A blue pool, a waterfall, and the Black Cuillin behind it. Honestly the water's so clear you can see every rock. Which makes it worse. You know how far you have to climb out.

wild_camper.text: Scottish access law lets you camp almost anywhere, as long as you leave no trace. No trace means no trace. Pack your rubbish. Don't light a fire. Be nice to the sheep.
I came for a night. That was three weeks ago. The midges are the real landlords. I pay in blood.
